title: Verify and gate PathPilot mill-mode G54.1 P, G95, G96 CSS, and G33 threading

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
PathPilot Mill (`UM10587` Ch. 10) and the LinuxCNC G-code reference document extended work offsets (`G54.1 P1`..`P500`), feed per revolution (`G95`), constant surface speed (`G96 D S`), and spindle-synchronized threading (`G33 Z K`). On LinuxCNC, `G96` measures radius strictly from active WCS `X0` (never `Y`), and `G95`, `G96`, and `G33` require spindle encoder feedback (`motion.spindle-speed-in`), which servo-spindle mills such as the Tormach 770MX (`rigid_tapping: true`) provide.

Verify these behaviours on PathPilot Hub (770MX SIM) and then extend `assets/posts/tormach-mill-turn-spindle.cps` and machine capability checks:

- Record PathPilot Hub readings for `G54.1 P` index mapping (`P1`..`P6` vs `G54`..`G59`, `P7`..`P9` vs `G59.1`..`G59.3`, `P10`..`P255`), `G43 H` persistence across WCS changes, `G95`, `G96 D S`, and `G33 Z K` in Mill mode.
- Widen `workOffsetMax` and `workOffsetName(n)` in the part-in-spindle post to emit `G54.1 P<n>` up to `255` (`crates/post/src/post/work_offset.rs::MAX_BOUND`) once verified.
- Enable `G96 D<cap> S<vc>` with `G95` only on X-axis stations of machines with spindle encoder feedback and an explicit RPM clamp `D = min(machine.spindle_max, tool.max_rpm, setup.workholding_max_rpm)`. Always restore `G97` and `G94` at section end.
- Refuse `G96` on Y-axis stations and refuse `G95`, `G96`, and `G33` on machines without spindle encoder feedback.
- Enable `G33 Z K` threading when the thread hand's spindle direction matches the station's allowed direction, and refuse any mismatch by name.

Done means: PathPilot Hub readings are recorded in the PR or decision file, golden `.nc` tests pin `G54.1 P`, gated `G96`/`G95`, and `G33` output, and refusal tests pin Y-axis `G96`, non-encoder machines, unclamped CSS, and mismatched thread hand.

Part of #2580
